notes.title: Polysomnography Report
notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Polysomnography Report
Date: 04/27/2025
Patient: Thomas Goyette, 82-year-old male

Diagnostic in-laboratory polysomnography performed 04/27/2025. The study evaluated sleep patterns and breathing abnormalities throughout the night. Total apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) 44.9 events/hour. Central and mixed apneas comprised 13% of all events. Sleep architecture showed normal distribution of sleep stages with no unusual disruptions. These findings indicate severe sleep apnea with a notable component of central and mixed apneas. Clinical correlation and consideration of treatment options are advised.

Sleep Medicine Consultation
Date: 07/20/2026
Patient: Thomas Goyette, 83-year-old male

Reason for Consultation:
Evaluation and management of sleep-disordered breathing.

History:
Mr. Goyette is an 83-year-old male with a history of obstructive sleep apnea currently treated with CPAP therapy. He reports ongoing symptoms despite adherence to therapy.

Physical Examination:
BMI 30.9 kg/m2.

Sleep Study and CPAP Data:
CPAP failure: residual AHI 25.1 events/hour on CPAP at 10 cmH2O despite consistent nightly use.

Assessment:
The patient demonstrates persistent moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea despite adequate CPAP therapy and compliance.

Plan:
1. Consider alternative treatment options including bilevel positive airway pressure or advanced modalities.
2. Reassess mask fit and pressure settings.
3. Schedule follow-up sleep study to evaluate response to therapy adjustments.
4. Continue monitoring symptoms and adherence.

Summary:
Mr. Goyette remains symptomatic with significant residual apnea events on CPAP. Further evaluation and treatment modification are warranted to improve sleep quality and reduce apnea burden.
